problem: backend/data/iv_history.json is corrupt at line 24789 — two ISO timestamps are concatenated ("...019920+00:00""...139344+00:00"), the signature of two processes truncate-then-writing the same path concurrently. IvHistoryStore._read calls json.load with no try/except, so every read raises JSONDecodeError. _build_universe calls iv_store.append inside the per-symbol loop with no guard, and generate_recommendations does not wrap _build_universe, so the exception escapes the whole cycle. On Monday 2026-08-10 the scheduler's _entry_tick would raise on the first enriched symbol with IV>0, be swallowed by TradingScheduler._loop's broad handler, and — because _last_generation_at is stamped BEFORE the call — retry only once per 600s cadence. Result: roughly 31 identical failed attempts across the 09:20-14:30 entry window, zero recommendations, zero trades, scheduler stuck in 'degraded'. The store is also never pruned (1609 keys across 8 session dates, 814KB) and is fully rewritten on every single append, which widens the interleave window that caused the corruption in the first place.
proposed_change: Three changes, all in backend/services/iv_history_store.py. (1) Wrap json.load in try/except (OSError, ValueError) returning {} — the same guard ConfidenceCalibrator.reload already uses at confidence_calibrator.py:29-34, so this is an existing house pattern, not a new one. (2) Make _write atomic: json.dump to a sibling .tmp in the same directory then os.replace onto the target, so a reader never observes a half-written file and two writers cannot interleave mid-object. (3) Prune keys older than N session dates on write to stop the O(n) full-file rewrite from growing without bound. Separately, delete the currently corrupt backend/data/iv_history.json (it is gitignored runtime state, regenerated from the first cycle) — but do not treat deletion as the fix; without (1) and (2) the same corruption recurs.

expected_impact.rationale: Cycles currently complete at a rate of 0 whenever this file is corrupt, because the exception escapes _build_universe and aborts generation. Guarding the read makes a corrupt store degrade to an empty IV series (iv_z_score simply unusable, vega_scalping ineligible) instead of killing the cycle. Reliability counters accrue tens of events per session, so this one is measurable within a single trading day — unlike anything P&L-shaped.

problem: backend/services/learning_service.py carries the identical defect class as iv_history_store, on a strictly more valuable file. _read (lines 305-310) calls json.load unguarded and _write (lines 313-315) does a plain truncate-then-write with no atomicity or locking. learning_store.json is the trade ledger — it is where register_open_trade persists the one-trade lock and where record_ledger_close writes realized P&L. Corrupting it does not merely lose data: get_active_trade_id -> list_open_trades -> _read raises uncaught inside TradingScheduler._entry_tick, killing cycles exactly as the IV store does; and effective_min_confidence catches the exception and silently fails closed from the 0.70 bootstrap floor to the 0.80 config floor, so the engine would quietly get stricter with no operator-visible signal. The IV store has already demonstrated that concurrent truncate-then-write corrupts a file in this deployment, which is the evidence that this one is exposed too.
proposed_change: Apply the same atomic-write helper to LearningService._write (tmp file in the same directory + os.replace). Do NOT add a bare try/except returning {} to LearningService._read — silently substituting an empty store would erase trade history and unlock the one-trade scope. Instead, on a decode error, preserve the damaged file to a .corrupt sidecar, raise a typed LearningStoreError, and let effective_min_confidence keep failing closed to 0.80 while the scheduler surfaces the condition in last_error rather than an anonymous tick_error.

expected_impact.rationale: Same failure mechanism as the IV store — an unguarded read inside the entry tick aborts the cycle. Framed on cycles_completed because that is the counter that actually moves and reaches a usable sample within one session; the P&L consequence of losing the ledger is real but unmeasurable at n=0 real trades and should not be claimed as the metric.

notes: Not yet observed failing — proposed on demonstrated mechanism in a sibling store, not on an incident. Flagged as such deliberately.
The asymmetric fix (guard the IV store, do not guard the learning store) is the point: a regenerable cache should degrade to empty, a financial ledger must never silently do so.

problem: _history_for returns an empty close list when the shared generation deadline expires (recommendation_engine.py:378-379) and fetch_daily_closes returns [] on any Breeze exception (candle_history.py:65-67). Both are indistinguishable downstream from 'this symbol genuinely has no history': build_quant_snapshot sees a short series, sets garch_forecast unusable with reason 'insufficient_or_flat_history', and strategy_coverage then rules the symbol ineligible for all three strategies. The 90s generation_budget_sec is shared between enrichment and candle history, and enrichment runs first — 15 symbols x (spot + chain) at min_interval_ms=700 consumes a large fraction of it before a single candle is fetched, after which the remaining symbols silently lose GARCH. A coverage abort produced this way is reported with the same wording as a genuine data gap, so the operator cannot tell 'the market had no data' from 'we ran out of time'.
proposed_change: Distinguish the three cases at the source. Have _history_for return a typed reason ('budget_exhausted' | 'fetch_failed' | 'empty') alongside the series, propagate it into SignalField.reason, and count it in EnrichmentStats so the metrics row can carry reliability.coverage_abort_reasons as a real mix rather than a single opaque bucket. Give candle history its own sub-budget carved out of generation_budget_sec so enrichment cannot starve it.

expected_impact.rationale: Cannot promise the abort count falls on attribution alone — attribution is diagnostic, not curative. The falsifiable part is the sub-budget: if aborts are currently driven by starved candle fetches, reserving budget for them lowers the count; if aborts persist at the same rate with a clean reason mix, that falsifies the hypothesis and is itself the useful result. Judge this one on the reason mix first and the abort count second.

problem: IvHistoryStore is keyed SYMBOL|session_date and compute_iv_zscore is fed only the current session's samples, with iv_zscore.min_observations=5. Samples accrue one per symbol per recommendation cycle, and the scheduler cadence is 600s. So iv_z_score cannot become usable before the 5th cycle — roughly 09:20 + 40-50 minutes. eligible_vega_scalping requires iv_z_score.usable, so vega_scalping is structurally ineligible for the first ~50 minutes of every session and its coverage is 0/15, guaranteeing a STRATEGY_COVERAGE_ABORT for that strategy every morning. Worse, once it does warm up, the z-score is computed over 5 same-session observations, which is far too small a window to identify a -2.0 sigma IV flush with any statistical meaning; the threshold implies a distributional claim the sample cannot support.
proposed_change: Let compute_iv_zscore consume a cross-session ATM IV baseline (mean/sd from the trailing N session dates already sitting in the same store — 8 dates and 213 symbols are present today) while continuing to use the live sample as the current observation. That makes the z-score meaningful from the first cycle of the session and removes the daily cold-start abort. Keep a minimum baseline-observation count so a genuinely new symbol still reports unusable rather than a spurious z.

expected_impact.rationale: vega_scalping contributes a guaranteed abort in every cycle before warm-up; removing the cold start removes those aborts deterministically, which is countable within one session. The separate claim — that a cross-session z-score is a BETTER signal — is NOT covered by this metric and must not be inferred from an abort-count improvement. That claim needs OOS walk-forward evidence and is explicitly not being made here.

notes: The store already holds 213 symbols x 8 session dates, so the baseline data exists; only the key scheme and the query prevent using it.

problem: Two of the coverage relaxations interact in a way that makes one of them dead. evaluate_strategy_coverage publishes a strategy only when coverage >= min_coverage_ratio AND eligible >= min_eligible_symbols. scanned is EnrichmentStats.requested, which universe_enrichment sets to len(capped) — the max_symbols cap, i.e. 15 — not the full 213-name FNO universe. So the ratio test requires 0.60 x 15 = 9 eligible symbols, while min_eligible_symbols=6 requires 6. The ratio always binds harder, so min_eligible_symbols=6 has no effect at the current max_symbols and the real gate is 9 of 15. Anyone reasoning about Monday from the config file will believe the bar is 6 when it is 9.
proposed_change: No config change is being proposed here — the point is to make the effective bar legible before it is tuned. Emit the computed threshold (max(ceil(min_coverage_ratio * scanned), min_eligible_symbols)) in the STRATEGY_COVERAGE note line and in api_rows, so the abort message states the number that actually bound. Only once the effective bar is visible should the owner decide whether 9-of-15 is the intended strictness.

expected_impact.rationale: Direction 'up' means richer/attributable reason data, not more aborts — this change adds the binding threshold to the reason string. It deliberately does not claim to reduce aborts, because it changes no behavior. Recording it as an observability fix rather than a tuning win keeps it from being credited later for an improvement it cannot cause.

notes: max_symbols=15, min_coverage_ratio=0.60 and min_eligible_symbols=6 are test-scaffold values allowed only to probe whether a paper trade lands on 2026-08-10. They are open questions, not settled or owner-approved settings.

Trap to avoid on the next run: if a trade DOES land on 2026-08-10, that is evidence the end-to-end loop works. It is not evidence that 0.60/6/15 are correct values. Those two conclusions must stay separate.

problem: Confidence is computed as min(0.95, score + 0.05), then adjusted by a failure-memory penalty, then passed through ConfidenceCalibrator.apply. No calibration artifact exists (backend/data/confidence_calibration.json is absent), so apply returns the raw value with status 'uncalibrated' and source 'heuristic' for every recommendation. effective_min_confidence then gates on that number: the 0.70 bootstrap floor is, in practice, 'score >= 0.65 after learning penalty'. It is a rank-ordering statistic wearing probability clothing. The naming invites the owner to read 0.70 as a 70% win probability, which nothing in the pipeline currently supports, and the map can only be fitted from real closed outcomes — of which there are 0 — so the system cannot bootstrap out of this on its own.
proposed_change: Surface the distinction where the decision is made rather than only in the logic trail: have the recommendation payload and the decisions UI label an uncalibrated confidence explicitly as a heuristic score, and have effective_min_confidence return the calibration status alongside (floor, source) so the gate's own output records whether it compared against a calibrated probability or a score proxy. Defer any recalibration of the numeric floor until the outcome map can actually be fitted.

expected_impact.rationale: Honest framing: this change cannot reduce calibration error by itself — calibration error is currently undefined because there are zero real outcomes to compare predicted confidence against. The metric is named as the thing to watch once real closes exist; the near-term value is preventing a mis-read of the 0.70 floor. Do not mark this validated on any evidence short of a fitted outcome map with a real sample.

notes: Maturity gate: below ~30 real closed trades per module, no calibration verdict is available at all. Current real closed trades: 0.
